description.narrative:
Gender Budget Watchdog Network (GBWN) är ett nätverk av civilsamhällesorganisationer från västra Balkan och Moldavien som syftar till att förbättra civilsamhällets deltagande i policyprocesser och budgetprocesser i regionen genom att granska offentliga budgetar ur ett jämställdhetsperspektiv.
Målet med insatsen är att förbättra de offentliga åtagandena för jämställdhetsintegrerade klimatåtgärder och öka den tillgängliga finansieringen för att genomföra jämställdhetsintegrerade klimatåtgärder i västra Balkanregionen och Moldavien.
Nätverket samordnas av Centre for Research and Policy Making (CRPM), en icke-statlig regional organisation/tankesmedja med säte i Skopje. Sida finansierar 20% av GBWNs totala budget och resterande 80 % finansieras av Österrikes utvecklingsmyndighet ADA.

The Gender Budget Watchdog Network (GBWN) is a network of civil society organisations throughout the Western Balkans and Moldova which aims at improving civil society organizations' participation in policy and budgeting processes in the Western Balkans and Moldova by using gender budget watchdog reporting and networking.
The goal of the intervention is to improve public sector commitments for gender sensitive climate action and increase the available funding to implement gender-integrated climate action in the Western Balkans region and Moldova.
The network is coordinated by Centre for Research and Policy Making (CRPM), which is an NGO/think tank based in Skopje with a regional perspective. Sida is financing 20% of the total budget, and the other 80% is financed by the Austrian Development Agency.

The overall goal of the intervention is to improve public sector commitments for gender sensitive climate action and increase the available funding to implement gender-integrated climate action in the Western Balkans region and Moldova.
The goals of the program is:
i) Increased visibility and international recognition of the work carried out by the Gender Budget Watchdog Network
ii) Increased capacity of civil society organizations to use gender budget tools to monitor climate change policy and finance
iii) Improved participation of civil society organizations in policy and budget processes by using gender budgeting tools for monitoring for increased government accountability, especially regarding resilience, climate finance, and gender responsiveness and inclusion in the policy framework against climate change.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
Internationally, the Gender Budget Watchdog Network (GBWN) has become a more active actor (advocacy towards the UN system and using UN and other international for a for holding governments accountable of how they are spending money, participation through side events at Commission of Status of Women (CSW), cooperation with OECD has been established).
CSO's have gained capacity to monitor Gender-Responsive Budgeting (GRB). The network has contributed to increased capacity and knowledge among its members through courses and network events for civil society organisations (CSOs), e-learning, mentoring, sub-granting, and other communicative events.
Regional exchange and networking has taken place in accordance with the network development strategy through various network events for members. The network has also been engaged in advocacy and networking at the international level through participation in various international fora. It is not clear what this networking and exchange have led to.
Two research products have been published: Gender responsive budgeting: Delivering on gender equality commitments in multilaterals' external financing and Gender analysis of the transportation sector towards gender and climate-responsive policy solutions
The network awarded grants to civil society organisations for projects both on a regional and on a national level. Consolidated results from the grants are not yet reported.
The network detected several policy impact results at country level that the network has influenced through continued advocacy that commenced in the first phase of the project.
- In Albania the Ministry of Finance and Economy has responded to the advocacy claim of GBWN to publish Gender Responsive Budgeting programs for each ministry.
- In Bosnia and Herzegovina, the State Audit Institution conducted a Gender Audit in 2023.
- In Kosovo the Government finalized the Management Reform Strategy Public Finance 2022-2026 to which GBWN provided comments. The partner Kosovo Women's Network contributed to recommendations for the World Bank's new Gender Strategy for 2024-2030, collaborating with Kvinna till Kvinna and other CSOs in the Western Balkans to prepare joint input for the strategy as well as advocated for it.
- In Moldova the National Development Strategy "Moldova Europeana 2030" was adopted within which gender-responsive budgeting is considered an important method for promoting gender equality and a priority measure to implement the objectives of the Strategy. GBWN contributed to the development of the National Program for accelerating gender equality in the Republic of Moldova for the years 2023-2027.
- In Montenegro the State Audit institution has for the first time prepared an Audit of the success of the implementation of gender equality policy encompassing gender responsive budgeting.
- In North Macedonia, in February 2023 the changes of the Criminal Code aligning Macedonian legislation with Istanbul Convention were adopted, as well as the Law on Amendments and Supplements to the Law on Value Added Tax was sent to Parliament in July 2023, responding to the GBWN advocacy to decrease impact on menstrual poverty.
- In Serbia, a petition for reduction of VAT on menstrual product has been launched and so far, 48.038 signatures are collected. The petition is for the attention of the Minister of Finance, President of the Coordinating Body for Gender Equality and Prime Minister of Serbia.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
